sentences.text: The genus Dasosaurus contains only one known species, Dasosaurus tocantinensis.
Its holotype — the specimen the species is based on — represents a medium-to-large sauropod approximately 20 meters long.
This fossil includes limb bones, ribs, and at least ten disarticulated tail vertebrae.
Archaeologist Daniel Ribeiro da Silva discovered Dasosaurus fossils in Davinópolis, Maranhão, Brazil.
The discovery was announced in 2021 as a new titanosaur taxon.
The name Dasosaurus combines the Greek words for 'forest' and 'lizard', referencing the Amazon rainforest type locality.
The specific name tocantinensis honors the state of Tocantins, near the type locality.
Dasosaurus has a morphology similar to the European titanosauriform Garumbatitan.
Dasosaurus belongs to the class Saurischia.
It is classified as a sauropod belonging to the group Somphospondyli.
The parent group of Dasosaurus is Somphospondyli.
Dasosaurus lived during the Aptian stage, between 119.57 and 113.2 million years ago.
Researchers suggest Dasosaurus exhibits European affinities, indicating potential biogeographic connections between Brazil and Europe in the Early Cretaceous.
